title: Stackless vs. Stackful Coroutines: A Comparative Study for RDMA-based Asynchronous Many-Task (AMT) Runtimes
problem: Asynchronous Many-Task (AMT) runtimes manage fine-grained parallelism by suspending and migrating task continuations across processes via RDMA. The efficiency of continuation creation, context switching, and migration critically impacts application performance, but trade-offs between stackful and stackless coroutines for AMT are not systematically evaluated.
motivation: AMT runtimes are increasingly used for irregular, data-dependent computations on large clusters. Understanding coroutine implementation trade-offs (overhead, memory footprint, communication impact) is essential for runtime design and optimization.
method: The researchers built two versions of task-management systems that do the same job but use different approaches: one with traditional stackful coroutines (where each task gets its own memory stack) and one with C++20 stackless coroutines (a lighter approach that doesn't allocate full stacks). They tested both systems on work where tasks steal work from each other across a network (using RDMA, a fast way to access memory on other computers), running lots of small tasks that themselves spawn more tasks. They measured how fast each system could create new tasks, switch between them, how much memory each approach needs, and how long it takes to send work between computers.
key_novelty: This is the first head-to-head comparison of traditional stackful coroutines versus lightweight stackless coroutines in a distributed task system that uses RDMA networking, with detailed measurements of what each approach costs.
contributions: Comparative study of stackful and stackless coroutine implementations
Overhead analysis: creation, context switching, frame size
Communication impact assessment for both coroutine types
Guidelines for AMT runtime design decisions

metrics.communication_dominance: Network latency dominates, frame size reduction minimal for comm time

limitations: No evaluation on other workload patterns (coarse-grained, data-parallel)
Scalability beyond test cluster size not demonstrated
Task state complexity impact not fully characterized
primary_theme: Continuation Implementation Trade-offs in Distributed Runtimes
